lastCompletedStory.title: Enforce command-set exhaustiveness at compile time

nextStoryContext: index.ts now has `const COMMANDS = [...] as const` + `type Command = (typeof COMMANDS)[number]` (declared right before HELP_REGISTRY, ~index.ts:2372) as the single source of truth for the 26 current commands (init, setup, config, run, plan, spec, issue, next, review, ship, tag, dashboard, status, orch-budget, stop, drain, resume, claude, sidecar, orch-recycle-watch, sidecar-liveness-watch, retry-monitor, journal, patterns, triage, suggestions — the story text said '25', the actual count is 26; verified exact parity via test). HELP_REGISTRY is now `Record<Command, string>`. `isCommand(value: string): value is Command` narrows argv[2] BEFORE the dispatch switch; the 'unknown command: <cmd>' branch now lives right after that guard (not in the switch's default anymore). The switch's `default:` is now exhaustiveness-only: `const _never: never = command; throw new Error(...)` — unreachable at runtime, compile-time-only enforcement. Both COMMANDS and Command are exported from index.ts for tests. test/help-registry.test.ts gained a describe block asserting COMMANDS === HELP_REGISTRY keys and COMMANDS === every `case '<cmd>':` label (parsed via Bun.file + regex against the switch body text) — any future command must be added to all three (COMMANDS array, HELP_REGISTRY entry, switch case) or typecheck/this test fails. Manually verified (deletion + revert, not committed): removing a HELP_REGISTRY entry -> TS2741 'Property X is missing'; removing a switch case -> TS2322 'Type X is not assignable to type never'. Both confirm the enforcement is real, not cosmetic.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed the `const _never: never = command;` exhaustiveness-check pattern in the switch default case matches the TS handbook's canonical narrowing-with-never idiom exactly.
